public_functions.name: GNUNET_RESOLVER_disconnect

public_functions.name: GNUNET_RESOLVER_ip_get

public_functions.name: GNUNET_RESOLVER_hostname_get

public_functions.name: GNUNET_RESOLVER_hostname_resolve

public_functions.name: GNUNET_RESOLVER_request_cancel

globals: resolver_cfg is independent of CLIENT service cfg; borrowed identity must survive old MQ after selection replacement
one shared mq, req_head/tail FIFO, opaque native-endian last_request_id; numeric tasks also consume IDs
backoff starts1ms, reconnect schedules current then doubles max900s; connect resets value without rescheduling existing r_task
s_task idle shutdown after1ms, canceled on new remote request; shutdown resets1ms; explicit disconnect does not reset
fifo: Only head is submitted; submitted/canceled head blocks queued tail
Timeout can remove a head while its MQ envelope is still unsent; next head is then copied to same real MQ queue
Sent cancel suppresses every callback and waits for END/error/idle; no cancel protocol message
END of canceled request reclaims head then processes next; error removes canceled head then retries next
Queued requests have their own admission timeout, can expire before transmission; no restart of original deadlines
responses: Any known queued/submitted/canceled remote ID can be matched; no extra head-only or requested-AF filter
Forward payload only4/16 bytes; reverse last byte NUL required, visible value ends at first NUL, arbitrary non-UTF8 preserved
Empty8-byte response is END; reverse with no successful name first reports numeric fallback then finalNULL unless canceled in fallback
Malformed identified response terminates only that request and retires MQ; unknown ID retires MQ and retries original head unchanged
Unregistered message types ignored by MQ; short registered type5 is MQ error
Already received reverse-name state survives reconnect, suppresses later numeric fallback
fast: Forward numeric and localhost/ip6-localnet bypass cfg check and remain deferred even timeout0
Any-family loopback order isV6 thenV4; numeric preserves detected family
Reverse numeric requires current cfg; native sockaddr invalid lengths/family cannot be represented by typed IpAddr
Numeric tasks are not in remote DLL and survive explicit disconnect
configuration: check_config only tests UNIXPATH presence or numeric/known-loopback HOSTNAME, not full CLIENT endpoint validity
New Resolver MQ validates current selected cfg and caches TCP then; Unix retry rereads that MQ's original cfg identity
Changing selected cfg does not replace existing MQ/attempt; old store mutation can change only subsequent Unix attempts

PROGRAM scheduled main starts SPEEDUP, registers shutdown-stop, selects resolver before user main; direct mode selects before main without SPEEDUP; original C cleanup destroys cfg without clearing selected pointer
client: CLIENT caches service TCP PORT/HOSTNAME per MQ, reads UNIXPATH every even/no-TCP physical attempt
CLIENT lookup uses independent shared resolver_cfg, never service cstate->cfg
Every TCP address creates independent5s probe; first success cancels other probes but DOES NOT cancel dns_active
A connected service stream retains DNS subscription until actual END/timeout or destruction; later addresses ignored if sock exists
Native lookup returningNULL leaves CLIENT without probes/dns_active and does not itself call connect_fail_continuation; preserve/resolve this explicit profile branch rather than fabricate an END
clock: Context samples one explicit source clock at original admission; original deadline addition saturatesMAX
Driver registers clock revision changes and recalculates original logical deadlines; backwards adjustments allowed
Drive budget remains real Tokio time, independent of source speedup
Default monotonic profile and explicit PROGRAM clock adapter are distinct; actual clock/profile proof remains required
ownership: Only one driver; cloned contexts share core and MQ, no query-private socket
One callback Delivery lease blocks next callback/timer effect until return; caller can cancel/reconfigure via Context during callback
Name bytes copied into a preallocated reusable scratch lease before input buffer reuse; no UTF8 conversion
Bounded remote MQ credits reserved before admission cover live requests and expired orphan envelopes; queue cannot lose a marked submission or starve transport under full credit
Driver drop closes sockets and reports owner loss; it emits no fabricated public DNS terminal
